corrections.statement: prlimit --as takes BYTES. The red startup probe recorded in runs[2] used --as=393216, i.e. 393216 bytes = 384 KiB, NOT 384 MiB. A 384 KiB address-space cap is unattainable for any dynamically linked binary (the libc mapping alone exceeds it), so the SIGSEGV (exit 139, empty stdout/stderr) of '/bin/echo hi' and of 'python3 -I -c print' under that value is explained by the unit error in that probe alone.

invocation.harness_note: prlimit invoked directly from the session shell segfaults its child (exit 139, empty stdout/stderr) because that shell's VmSize is ~19 GiB, so the forked child inherits an address space already far above RLIMIT_AS and dies on exec. '/bin/echo hi' reproduces it identically under prlimit --as=402653184, and bare 'python3 -I -c print' does too, so the failure is a harness artifact independent of the tool and the case. exec'ing a small binary first (exec /usr/bin/timeout ...) shrinks the inherited address space and makes prlimit behave as specified; the equivalent ulimit -v 393216 run produced byte-identical stdout/stderr.
